A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new method for the evaluation of elastic coefficients of thin layers by resonant ultrasound spectroscopic (RUS) measurements, which is based on a linearized approximation of the RUS forward and inverse problems.

the linearized forward and inverse models of RAS for the evaluation of elastic properties of thin surface coatings are valid for the thickness range of about 200–400 nm and that the errors of the inversely determined coefficients can be estimated by the presented method.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the linearized inverse problem is a viable approach to determine elastic coefficients of thin surface layers, and that its applicability range can be extended by a careful choice of the measurement geometry and the frequency range.
the linearized forward and inverse procedures are valid for thin layers of a thickness of the order of the wavelength in the material, provided that the material is not too stiff.

linearized models of the forward problem are applicable for thin surface layers with a thickness less than 10% of the wavelength, and that linearized models can be used to estimate elastic coefficients of thin surface layers with an error of about 5% in comparison with nonlinear models.
